name: LinkedIn Profile Analysis - API Designer
description: Signals extracted from LinkedIn profiles to evidence API Designer skills. LinkedIn provides professional context, endorsements, recommendations, and career progression data. Focus on API architecture, governance, and platform design leadership roles.

sections.notes: Self-described; provides intent and specialization context (e.g., 'API Architect' or 'API Platform Engineer' vs generic 'Software Engineer').

sections.description: Work experience entries with job titles, companies, and responsibilities.
sections.notes: Look for API-specific titles and descriptions of governance scope, platform architecture, and standards leadership.
quality_indicators: API-specific job titles (API Architect, API Platform Engineer, API Product Manager, Developer Experience Lead)
Duration and continuity in API governance or platform roles
Company scale and API platform complexity (large enterprise with hundreds of APIs vs startup)
Specific governance outcomes described (style guides adopted, developer portal launched, design review process established)

sections.description: Skills listed with endorsement counts from connections.
sections.notes: Endorsements have very low evidential value on their own. They provide a high-level self-reported technology inventory.
Theoretical domain indicator, not practical governance proof.

sections.description: Projects section with descriptions and links.
sections.notes: Provides additional project context. Links to published API style guides, open-source governance tools, or developer portals increase strength.

sections.description: Written recommendations from engineering leaders, API consumers, or platform team peers.
sections.notes: Third-party validation of API governance leadership, standards quality, and developer experience impact.

sections.description: Technical posts and articles published on LinkedIn.
sections.notes: Articles about API design philosophy, governance patterns, or protocol selection indicate deep API architecture grasp.

signal_mapping.description: How LinkedIn mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: LinkedIn skills endorsement for 'API Design' or 'REST APIs'
LinkedIn skills endorsement for 'OAuth2' or 'API Security'
Job experience explicitly describing API governance, style guide authoring, or design review processes
Job experience describing API platform architecture with gateway strategy and contract testing
Job experience describing developer portal design and API onboarding optimization
Job experience describing API performance engineering with SLOs and capacity planning
Job experience describing OAuth2 scope design and API authentication architecture
Technical article about API design patterns, governance, or protocol selection trade-offs

important_notes: ALL extracted signals MUST be mapped to COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id})
LinkedIn data supplements but should not override verified governance artifacts or assessment evidence
Endorsements have near-zero evidential value on their own
Job titles can be inflated — cross-reference with actual governance scope and architectural responsibilities described
Career trajectory (progression from API implementer to API architect to API platform leader) provides valuable context
Specialized API governance content (published style guides, design review processes, protocol selection frameworks) indicates advanced seniority
Distinguish between 'built APIs' (backend developer work) and 'governed APIs' (API designer work) in experience descriptions
